answer: Each epoch the network posts a cryptographic challenge that forces the agent to produce a fresh Falcon‑style inference chain, whose answer must ripple through a Merkle tree of recent state. The seed is a deterministic spiral of prior block hashes, so replayed proofs fail and every new identity must spend fresh model compute to solve it. An attacker therefore pays the full GPU cost for each bogus ID each epoch, making a Sybil attack economically prohibitive.
